subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Nancy Roman: Mother of Hubble
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nancy Roman: Mother of Hubble.

hook.text: Nancy Roman was NASA's first Chief of Astronomy. She championed the space telescope that became Hubble.

buildup.text: In the 1960s, she argued that a telescope above Earth's atmosphere would revolutionize astronomy. NASA listened.

discovery.text: She oversaw the planning and advocacy that made the Hubble Space Telescope possible, fighting for funding for decades.

twist.text: When Hubble launched in 1990, its mirror was flawed. Astronauts fixed it in 1993—and it became the most famous telescope ever.

climax.text: Hubble has produced over 1.5 million observations, revealing the age, size, and expansion rate of the universe.

punchline.text: She fought for a telescope in space. It changed everything we know.

quiz.question: Why is Nancy Roman called the 'Mother of Hubble'?
options: She championed and oversaw the planning of the Hubble Space Telescope at NASA
She was the first person to observe through the Hubble telescope
She designed the mirror that was installed in Hubble

details.summary: Nancy Grace Roman (1925-2018) was NASA's first Chief of Astronomy and the driving force behind the Hubble Space Telescope's development. She convinced Congress and NASA leadership that a space telescope was scientifically essential and technically feasible, earning her the title 'Mother of Hubble.'
details.whyItMatters: Roman's advocacy and organizational leadership made Hubble possible. Her career demonstrated that pioneering science requires not just brilliant ideas but also determined advocates who can navigate politics and bureaucracies to make them reality.
takeaways: Roman was NASA's first Chief of Astronomy
She championed and secured funding for the Hubble telescope
NASA's Roman Space Telescope is named in her honor

faq.question: What challenges did Roman face as a woman in astronomy?
faq.answer: She was told by a college counselor that women 'don't do' science. Academic positions for women were severely limited — many universities wouldn't hire female astronomers. She joined NASA partly because government positions were more open to women than academia in the 1950s-60s.

faq.question: What is the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope?
faq.answer: A NASA flagship observatory planned for launch in the mid-2020s. It has a field of view 100 times wider than Hubble's at similar resolution. Its primary missions include studying dark energy, discovering exoplanets, and surveying the infrared universe — extending Roman's scientific legacy.
